recap:
Joe sits down with Brigham Buhler, founder of Ways2Well and cofounder of ReviveRx, to dive into the world of functional and regenerative medicine. Buhler brings a perspective that challenges a lot of conventional healthcare thinking, focusing on treating the actual root causes of health problems instead of just masking symptoms with standard pharmaceutical approaches.

The conversation centers around how modern medicine often falls short because it's built on a system designed to treat acute problems and disease management rather than optimizing human health and longevity. Buhler explains how his clinics operate differently, using functional medicine protocols that dig deeper into what's actually causing someone's health issues. The discussion gets into the real gaps in conventional care and how that's created an opportunity for clinics like Ways2Well to serve patients who feel like they're not getting real answers from their traditional doctors.

ReviveRx comes up as a natural extension of this philosophy, providing compounded medications and formulations that aren't available through standard pharmacy chains. Buhler talks about how personalized medicine and customized dosing can make a huge difference for patients who don't respond well to one-size-fits-all pharmaceutical solutions. The conversation touches on the business side of healthcare too, discussing how the current system creates perverse incentives and why regenerative medicine represents a different way of thinking about health entirely.

Throughout the episode, Buhler demonstrates genuine passion for actually helping people get better, not just dependent on medications. Joe and Brigham explore the philosophy behind functional medicine, how it differs from conventional approaches, and why more people aren't aware of these options. It's a substantive conversation about healthcare transformation and what the future of medicine might look like when practitioners focus on restoration and optimization rather than just disease management.
